key_insight: FracLearn shows that a language model can improve physical design by turning simulated fracture experience into reusable rules, then applying those rules to create stronger new architectures without changing model weights.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path for AI-assisted materials and structural design where models learn toughening strategies from experiments or simulations and transfer them to future design problems.
method: Generate candidate architectures in a fracture-inspired game
Abstraction converts outcomes into conditional principles for crack behavior and load transfer
Generalization recombines learned principles to design improved architectures
evidence_signal: Across campaigns, the best design achieved a composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record, with fracture analysis linking gains to crack deflection, temporary crack trapping, and higher residual load capacity.
watch_item: The approach was demonstrated in a deliberately unfamiliar simulated game, so transfer to real materials systems may require careful validation and domain-specific setup.
paper_title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
